problem: The sentence "The order matters in non-abelian groups" uses the technical word "order" ambiguously. In this chapter "order" means the size of a group or the order of an element, so a student may think the size of the group matters, not the order of the factors in ab.
fix: "The order of the factors matters: in a non-abelian group ab and ba can be different."

problem: Sₙ and the sign of a permutation are used without a local definition or link. A phone reader may not recall what Sₙ is or what sign(σ) means, so the example and the quiz answer are hard to follow.
fix: Add one line: Sₙ is the group of all permutations of n symbols under composition, and sign(σ)=+1 for even permutations and −1 for odd permutations; or link to the chapter where they are defined.

problem: The chapter writes the quotient multiplicatively as (aH)(bH)=abH, then switches to additive notation r+6Z in the worked example without saying that Z is written additively. Students may not see that the two notations describe the same quotient construction.
fix: Add: "Z is an additive group, so we write cosets as r+6Z and the operation as (r+6Z)+(s+6Z)=(r+s)+6Z; this is the same coset construction as aH above."

problem: "Monoid" is used in the ring definition without a definition. The chapter also does not state that it requires a multiplicative identity, while some textbooks define rings without unity.
fix: Define monoid as a set with an associative product and an identity, and state: "Here a ring has a multiplicative identity 1; some textbooks allow rings without 1."

problem: The notation H ≤ G and G\H is not explained in the quiz answers.
fix: Write "H is a subgroup of G (H ≤ G)" and "G\H means the set of elements of G not in H" at first use.

problem: "Kernels are always normal subgroups, meaning gHg⁻¹=H" omits the quantifier "for every g ∈ G"; the condition is not a single conjugation.
fix: "Kernels are always normal subgroups: for H=ker f, gHg⁻¹=H for every g ∈ G."

problem: The search term "GF(2^8)" uses a caret instead of the Unicode superscript used elsewhere; it may also be read as 2 to the power 8 rather than the field with 256 elements.

The section on rings and fields is off-topic for a chapter titled "Normal subgroups and group homomorphisms"; it is marked optional, but it still sits in the exam chapter and can distract a student revising groups.
fix: Move the definitions to the rings-and-fields chapter or a clearly separated appendix; keep only a one-line pointer here.
